text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The consultant engaged to design and build the Lake Chini dam had disregarded a recommendation in the project's environmental impact assessment on the height of the dam. The increase of the dan's height to 3.12 metres from 1.8 metres has caused floods in the surrounding area, the Cabinet was told.
-- In a move to ensure that the private sector does not sponsor overseas trips as a way to obtain favours, the government has banned staff of local authorities from going on such trips.

-- The Malaysian business community seems to be relatively unconcerned over the threat of the Millennium Bug, a problem caused by the inability of computer software to recognise the year 2000 in its date-keeping functions, according to a software specialist.
-- The Cabinet has directed all states to set up action committees to combat the spread of dengue following a sharp rise in the numbers of cases reported all over the country.
-- The Selangor Religious Department has started enforcing laws against Moslems who dress indecently in public places.

-- Rights issues, traditionally the favoured means of raising capital, do not appear to have lost much of their appeal among the companies despite the bearish market situation in the first half of the year.
-- Except for the Infrastructure Project Companies and Trusts, the market capitalisation of all other sectors of the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange as at June 30 1997 showed a decline.
